newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs end up with Bunds, shrug off Belgian budget.
newsitem.headline: OLOs end up with Bunds, shrug off Belgian budget.

text.p: With the official unveiling of the 1997 Belgian budget springing no surprises, Belgian bonds ended at the day's best levels after climbing steadily in the afternoon with Bunds on weaker-than-expected U.S. NAPM data.
The essence of Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaeane's budget, which promises to get Belgium in shape to join a single European currency, had been leaked last week.

"There were no surprises, but the spread over Bunds remains narrow, as there was no profit-taking afterwards," one dealer said. The 2006 OLO yield was 6.19 percent at the close, down from 6.23 percent on Monday and its spread stable at 13 bp.
In the money markets three month T-bill yields were barely changed at the close, quoting at 3.02/07 percent after an average yield at Tuesday's weekly T-bill auction of 3.04 percent.
One week repo rates, which represent market expectations for the Belgian National Bank's 3.00 percent central rate, were unchanged at 3.01/03 percent.
The franc held steady to the mark at 20.5870/80.
